newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends mixed, AGAs seen neutral.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends mixed, AGAs seen neutral.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended mixed Wednesday in a moderate session, with front months losing ground early, then showing little reaction on ACCESS following weekly AGA data, industry sources said.

April skidded 10.4 cents to close at $1.839 per million British thermal units, then on ACCESS traded on either side of unchanged. May settled 7.7 cents lower at $1.902. Other deferreds ended mixed, with some late 1998s scoring gains.
"It's (AGAs) within the range. It was already in the market and it's not having any impact (on ACCESS)," said one East Coast trader, noting futures sold off early on weather.
AGA said U.S. gas stocks fell last week by 76 bcf, in line with expectations, but were still 130 bcf, or 15 percent, above year-ago. Eastern storage was still 198 bcf, or 53 percent, over last year.
Technically, traders said the market remained range-bound, with April support still at $1.78, then in the mid-$1.70s and at the contract low of $1.701. Resistance was seen at $1.965 and then $2.04.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices gained about five cents Wednesday to the $1.90 level. Midcon pipes were up a dime to the low-$1.80s. New York city gate swing gas firmed about 10 cents to the $2.20 area.
The 12-month strip slipped 5.7 cents to $2.031. NYMEX said an estimated 44,140 Hub contracts traded, up slightly from Tuesday's revised tally of 43,267.
NYMEX Permian and Alberta natgas did not trade Wednesday.

On the KCBT, April finished 12 cents lower at $1.59, while deferreds ended down by five to eight cents. The East/West spread widened by 1.6 cents to 24.9 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 666 lots changed hands, up from Tuesday's total of 412.
